Just like the original Fakin' It , players have the goal of finding the Faker amongst their room each question. Unlike the original, this game has both the addition of remote-play and character avatars for each person. All of the characters are in their swimwear in this game, unlike the original.

 Avatars marked with an asterisk are original avatars returning from the original game.

 Gameplay [ ] 

 The game is played in four rounds, with the first three being selected by the players from a pool of five categories and the fourth being a special category called Text You Up. In each round, the players are given a secret task that they must complete except for one, who is simply told that they are the Faker. The Faker must try their best to blend in with the rest of the group or risk being found out. Each round consists of three tasks, and in most categories, players vote for the Faker after each task. This game differs from the original in that the Faker is told they are the Faker except for the final round. This game also no longer requires votes for the Faker to be unanimous, only requiring more than half the room voting for the same person to reach a consensus (ex. In a room of eight players, five votes are required to reach a majority). The categories are as follows.

 Categories marked with an asterisk are original categories returning from the original game. 

 Hands of Truth* [ ] 

 Players are given a question that usually asks them whether or not they've done a certain thing and must raise their hand if the statement applies to them. In remote play, the players use their devices to make their on-screen characters raise their hands. When the game is played for the first time, Cookie automatically chooses this category as the first round.

 You Gotta Point* [ ] 

 Players are given a question where the answer is another player and must point at the player they think best fits the question. In remote play, this involves selecting a player on your device.

 Finger Blast* [ ] 

 Known as "Number Pressure" in the original game. Players are given a question where the answer is a number and must hold up a number of fingers for their answer, usually from zero to five (with the exception of one prompt that presumably only appears in in-person play that reads "Give everyone the middle finger. Because you're a bad boy!"). In remote play, players select a number of fingers for their on-screen character to hold up. (A small button on the bottom-right of the screen with a bird allows for you to give the middle finger.)

 Thumb Shot [ ] 

 Players are asked three questions in a row with two possible answers. They then must give a thumbs-up or thumbs-down for each one with the thumbs-up representing one answer (Ex. "Smash") and the thumbs-down representing the other (Ex. "Pass"). Once everyone's answers have been revealed for all three prompts, players then vote for the Faker.

 Emojional Damage* [ ] 

 Known as "Face Value" in the original game. Players are given a question that requires them to select an emoji. A search bar and list of emojis are presented on screen in remote play.

 Text You Up* [ ] 

 Always the final round. Players are given three questions that they must write answers to via text. Everyone's answers for all three questions are shown, and players only vote once for the Faker after answers for the third question are shown. This is the only round where the Faker is not told they are the Faker.

 Scoring [ ] 

 Players are awarded points after each round, depending on their performance. The player with the most points at the end of the game is the winner. The game also reveals the Best Faker (scored the most points as the Faker) and the Best Sleuth (scored the most points from choosing the Faker). The scoring is as follows: 

 Sleuth Bonus (correctly selecting the Faker, regardless of whether anyone else did): starts at 100 points for the first correct guess, but increases by 25 with each subsequent correct guess (125 for the second and 150 for the third)

 Caught Bonus: If the majority correctly guesses the Faker, all players who voted correctly get a Sleuth Bonus plus five additional points. This bonus varies depending on how many tasks it takes the group to catch the Faker.
 If they catch the Faker on the first task, everyone who guessed correctly gets 375 points.

 If they catch the Faker on the second task, those guessing correctly for the first time get 250 points, and those guessing correctly the second time get 275 points.

 If they catch the Faker on the third task, the points are scaled the same way as a Sleuth bonus but with five points added (105 for those guessing correctly the first time, 130 for the second time, and 155 for the third time)

 Faker Bonus: The Faker gets points for avoiding getting selected by the majority. The points are the same as the Sleuth Bonus: 100 points for getting away the first time, 125 points for the second time, and 150 points if they make it through all three tasks without getting caught.

 In Text You Up, players are still able to select which player they think is the Faker after the first and second questions without it being an official vote, so the same scoring still applies. In Thumb Shot, where there is only one vote, the Faker gets a 150-point Faker Bonus for getting away, non-Faker players get a 100-point Sleuth Bonus for correctly selecting the Faker when the Faker got away, and the majority can get a 150-point Caught Bonus for catching the Faker.

 Fakin' It All Night Long (stylized as Fakin' It! All Night Long ) is a social deduction video game and one of three games featured in The Jackbox Naughty Pack . It is the sequel to Fakin' It .

 The game works similar to the original: A random player is selected as the Faker, of which the other players (aka sleuths) attempt to find out who they are by answering prompts, then voting on who's answers seem off.

 Gameplay

 When you first enter the lobby through the player device, you can select from one of ten different avatars: Red Guy , Green Girl , Orange Guy , Blue Girl , Yellow Guy , and Purple Girl all return from the original, but are now playable characters. The remaining four avatars are brand new: Pink Dog , Gray Cat , Robot , and Teal Person .

 There are two different modes of gameplay: Same Room and Remote Play . Either one can be chosen directly from the game's main menu screen.

 Same Room

 HEADS UP! This page is under construction. 

 Pardon our dust—not all information is available. 

 Remote Play

 All inputs given from the game are shown on the player's device. After all inputs are received, the answers are then shown on the game's screen.

 At the beginning of each round, there are five categories to choose from:

 Hands of Truth : You're given your prompt (or a "blend in" text, if you're the Faker) and two buttons on your device: one to raise your hand, and one to not.

 You Gotta Point : You're given your prompt (or a "blend in" text, if you're the Faker) and a list of buttons featuring names from everyone currently in the game's room, including yourself.

 Emojional Damage: A more streamer-friendly version of the original game's "Face Value," where you're given your prompt (or a "blend in" text, if you're the Faker) and a board of emojis that are separated into their usual categories (faces, animals, objects, etc.)

 Finger Blast : A remade version of the original game's "Number Pressure," where you're given your prompt (or a "blend in" text, if you're the Faker) and 6 primary buttons, 6 of each containing fingers raised from 0 to 5. There is also a small bird button located at the bottom-right corner of the player's device—when pressed, the player's character will "flip the bird" during the voting phase.

 Thumb Shot: A new category where you're given a short prompt on your screen (or a "blend in" text, if you're the Faker) and two buttons with the prompt's text on-screen (A.K.A "SEXY or NOT SEXY", for example.) This continues for three rounds.

 Unlike in the original, the game does NOT require a unanimous vote in order to catch the Faker—instead, only a majority vote is required (like 5 players for an 8-player game.)

 After a generated number of rounds are played, the players move on to the final round: Text You Up . Just like in the original, the players (including the Faker) are given three separate prompts that they'll have to answer, one by one. The Faker will also get three more vaguer prompts that they too have to answer, however (unlike in the original) the Faker does not immediately know they're even the Faker, until after all of their answers have been sent.

 During the voting phase, all three prompts are shown per voting round— the Faker is not revealed until after the third voting round.

 After all is said and done, the player with the most points at the end of the game wins.
